chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who guaranteed the debt of another man, then settled (compounded) on part of what he had settled on. He said: 'There is upon him only what he settled on.'

key_terms.صَالَحَ: settled / compounded (agreed on a reduced amount to clear the debt)

ai.seo_question: What is the liability of a guarantor after settling a debt?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a guarantor (*damin*) who reaches a settlement (*sulh*) with the creditor is bound only by the agreed-upon terms, effectively capping his liability regardless of the original debt's magnitude. This ruling underscores the principle of contractual autonomy in Shia jurisprudence, where the mutual agreement supersedes the initial guarantee obligation. It provides practical legal certainty for guarantors engaging in debt restructuring or partial payment agreements.
